holidays.name: National White Wine Day
holidays.description: Pour something crisp and chilled. This day is for Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Grigio and every pale, bubbly or zesty bottle in between. It's the unofficial toast to summer sipping.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It lands in peak summer, when chilled white wine is at its most popular.
holidays.funFact: White wine can be made from red grapes. Most grape juice is clear, and the color of red wine comes from the skins being left in during fermentation.

holidays.name: National Psychic Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate fortune tellers, tarot readers, palm readers and anyone who claims to sense what's coming. You could get a reading, shuffle a tarot deck or just guess what your friends will say next. You probably already knew you'd read this.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's a playful nod to the long tradition of divination and psychic readings.
holidays.funFact: Tarot cards began as a card game in 15th-century Italy. They were not used for fortune telling until later.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Chip Cookie Day
holidays.description: A salute to the gooey, golden, chocolate-studded classic. Bake a batch, argue about chewy versus crispy and dunk them in milk without guilt.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors the chocolate chip cookie, which Ruth Wakefield is credited with creating at the Toll House Inn in Massachusetts in the 1930s.
holidays.funFact: The chocolate chip cookie is the official state cookie of Massachusetts, where it was reportedly invented.
